business_model.claim: DiamondRock Hospitality is a lodging REIT that owns premium hotels and resorts; as owner it receives all operating profits or losses from its hotels after paying fees to third-party hotel managers and, in certain cases, brand franchisors.
quotes: We are an owner, as opposed to an operator, of the hotels in our portfolio. As an owner, we receive all operating profits or losses generated by our hotels after we pay fees to the hotel managers, which are based on the revenues and profitability of the hotels, and the hotel brands, in certain cases, which are based on the revenues of the hotels.

business_model.claim: The company's revenue is derived from three hotel operating departments: Rooms, Food and Beverage, and Other (parking, spa, resort fees, guest services, tenant leases), sold to hotel guests and transient travelers.
quotes: Our revenue is primarily derived from hotel operations, including but not limited to rooms revenue, food and beverage revenue and other operating revenue, which consists of parking, spa, resort fees, other guest services, and tenant leases.

business_model.claim: Revenue growth is driven by two primary operating levers: Average Daily Rate (ADR) and Occupancy, which together determine RevPAR and Total RevPAR.
quotes: RevPAR, which is calculated as the product of ADR and occupancy percentage, and Total RevPAR, which is calculated as total revenues divided by room nights available, are important statistics for monitoring operating performance at the individual hotel level and across our portfolio.

business_model.claim: In Q3 2026, comparable portfolio ADR was $290.46 and occupancy was 77.8%, producing a comparable RevPAR of $226.01 and comparable Total RevPAR of $344.13.

competitive_position.claim: DRH's premium full-service hotel concentration makes it more volatile than other REITs: the segment historically delivers the strongest results in a growing economy and the weakest in a contracting or slow-growth economy, when travelers may curtail travel or choose lower-cost hotels.
quotes: our hotels are mostly in the premium full-service segment of the hotel business, which, historically, tends to have the strongest operating results in a growing economy and the weakest results in a contracting or slow growth economy when many travelers might curtail travel or choose lower cost hotels.

competitive_position.claim: DRH faces competition from alternative lodging channels including Airbnb and peer-to-peer platforms, as well as from third-party internet travel intermediaries such as Expedia and Priceline, which may negotiate higher commissions and put downward pressure on rates.
quotes: In addition to competing with traditional hotels and lodging facilities, we compete with alternative lodging, including third-party providers of short-term rental properties and serviced apartments, such as Airbnb, as well as alternative meeting and event space platforms, such as Convene.

Many of our managers and franchisors contract with third-party internet travel intermediaries, including, but not limited to, Expedia.com and Priceline.com, to sell rooms to leisure travelers, as well as for corporate and group travel.

competitive_position.claim: Because DRH must qualify as a REIT, it cannot operate or control the daily operations of its hotels; TRS lessees must engage third-party managers, and the company's ability to influence operations is limited to matters such as approval of the annual operating budget.
quotes: In order to qualify as a REIT, we cannot operate our hotel properties or control the daily operations of our hotel properties and therefore our TRS lessees must enter into third-party hotel management agreements with one or more eligible independent contractors.
our ability to participate in operating decisions regarding our hotel properties is limited to certain matters, including approval of the annual operating budget.

risks.claim: DiamondRock's concentration in premium full-service hotels makes earnings highly vulnerable to economic contraction, when travelers shift to lower-cost alternatives and fixed operating costs compress margins.
quotes: our hotels are mostly in the premium full-service segment of the hotel business, which, historically, tends to have the strongest operating results in a growing economy and the weakest results in a contracting or slow growth economy when many travelers might curtail travel or choose lower cost hotels.
Travel demand remained strong through the first nine months of 2026, contributing to growth in occupancy, ADR and hotel revenues across many of our markets.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 risk factors; counter inferred from P4 operating data
risks.claim: Growing competition from alternative lodging (Airbnb, short-term rentals), online travel intermediaries, and AI-driven search could erode occupancy, rates, and franchise brand value across the portfolio.
quotes: In addition to competing with traditional hotels and lodging facilities, we compete with alternative lodging, including third-party providers of short-term rental properties and serviced apartments, such as Airbnb, as well as alternative meeting and event space platforms, such as Convene.

An increase in hotel reservations made through these companies, including those that deploy artificial intelligence or automated recommendation tools, such as Google, Apple, Amazon or Meta, may reduce the value of our franchise brands, which may negatively affect our average rates and revenues.

at any given time, investors may be disinterested in buying properties subject to a ground lease and may pay a lower price for such properties than for a comparable property owned in fee simple or they may not purchase such properties at any price.

risks.claim: Sustained adoption of video conferencing and hybrid work arrangements could structurally reduce business travel demand, particularly affecting the company's urban gateway hotels.
quotes: The increased use of video conferencing technology by businesses has resulted in decreased business travel as companies have leveraged the use of technologies that allow multiple parties from different locations to participate in virtual meetings without traveling to a centralized meeting location, such as our hotels.

To the extent that such technologies, or new technologies, continue to play a role in day-to-day business interactions and the necessity for business-related travel decreases, demand for hotel rooms may decrease, which may have a material adverse effect on our hotels, our results of operations and our financial condition.
